units: <cite ref="Zevachim 12b:8">Zeb. 12ᵇ</cite> <he>כולהו בחדא ש׳ וכ׳</he> they all stood in one line (were equal in rank and united).—Pl. <he>שִׁיטַּיָּא</he>, <he>שִׁיטַּיָּה</he>, <cite ref="U00732"><he>שִׁטַּ׳</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shevuot 6:2:4">Y. Shebu. VI, 37ᵃ</cite> bot., v. <cite ref="S00358"><he>קוּלְסִיתָא</he></cite>. Y. Gitt. V, 46ᵈ bot. <he>והוה … ביני ש׳ וכ׳</he> and R. Ḥ. wrote between the lines; a. e.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 9:1:16">Y. Ber. IX, 13ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>ר׳ יודן … אמר בשיטה אוחרי</he> R. J. … expressed the idea in a different way; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 9:1:16">ib.</cite> <he>ר׳ יודן … ש׳ אוחרי</he>.

<cite ref="Ketubot 17a:6">Keth. 17ᵃ</cite> <he>שִׁיטָּתֵיה לסבא</he> (<he>אהניא ליה</he>) his line of conduct (habit of participating in wedding ceremonies) benefited the old man (v. <cite ref="U00386"><he>שׁוֹטִיתָא</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 69a:2">B. Mets. 69ᵃ</cite> <he>לאו … אלא שִׁיטָּה איתמר</he> it was not quoted as a halakhah, but as a line of opinions (all of equal rank).

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 8:2:3">Y. Snh. VIII, beg. 26ᵃ</cite> <he>מחלפא שִׁיטָּתֵיה וכ׳</he> R. S. b. Laḳish’s principle is at variance with itself: here he says …, and there he says &c.; Y. Peah IV, 18ᵈ bot., sq.; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Ruth Rabbah 5:6">Ruth R. to II, 14</cite> <he>פתר בה שית ש׳</he> interpreted it in six ways.
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 2:6">Lev. R. s. 2</cite> <he>אמר תרתין ש׳</he> offered two modes of developing the same idea, v. <cite ref="U00883"><he>שִׁיטָּה</he> III</cite>.
